function: Learned refinement of the delay-Doppler channel estimate (CNN-BGRU with sliding window) after threshold estimation, then classical single-tap time-frequency MMSE equalization with self-interference tuning (pp. 2-4).
system: OTFS transmitter-receiver link, antenna array and RIS not described; 16-QAM, M=64 subcarriers, N=14 symbols, 10 MHz bandwidth, 5.9 GHz carrier, 300 to 700 km/h (p. 4).
method: Supervised deep learning: three CNN layers, bidirectional GRU and dense layers with sliding-window structure; MSE loss, Adam, 100 epochs, trained offline against ideal channel (pp. 3-4, Table I).
data_channel: Simulated doubly selective Rayleigh channels, EVA and ETU profiles, 300 to 700 km/h; 16000 training and 2000 testing samples; no public dataset or measurements (pp. 4-5).
test_conditions: Training SNR 30 dB; testing SNR 0 to 30 dB (p. 4). BER at 300, 500, 700 km/h in EVA and ETU; training speed and profile unstated (p. 4).
baselines: Non-learned: embedded-pilot DD scheme [3] and cross-domain TFDD [10]; learned: TF-domain scheme derived from LSTM-based estimator [5]; own ablations (pp. 4-5, Table II).
metrics: BER versus SNR and speed (Fig. 5a, 5b), NMSE versus SNR (Fig. 5c), FLOPs for online computing and offline training (Fig. 5d), complexity orders (Table II) (pp. 4-5).
complexity: Table II (p. 5): proposed DDTF online O(Mg N + Md N), offline training O(Mg^2 N^2 + Mg N); FLOPs compared with DD, TF and TFDD in Fig. 5d.
q1_support: p. 5: "Channel model = {EVA,ETU}". EVA and ETU are the 3GPP LTE extended vehicular and urban delay profiles, not TR 38.901; the paper names them without a citation and does not state the training channel; marked met under the other-standardized-model rule.
q2_support: p. 4: "we perform comparison about BER with velocities of {300, 500, 700} km/h, {EVA, ETU}, 16-QAM". Speed and profile sweeps are not stated to be held out of training; Table I (p. 4) trains at 30 dB and tests at 0 to 30 dB, an SNR sweep that does not count.
q3_support: p. 4: "our scheme performs better than benchmark schemes derived from [3], [5], and [10]"; p. 5: "LSTM-based time-frequency domain channel estimation for OTFS modulation". [3] and [10] are classical; [5] is an earlier learned estimator (offline training in Table II); compared on BER and NMSE (Fig. 5a, 5c).
q4_support: p. 5: "we perform calculations on FLOPs required by each method". Table II gives the order of the proposed DDTF, online O(Mg N + Md N) and offline training O(Mg^2 N^2 + Mg N); Fig. 5d compares FLOPs.
q5_support: p. 4: "a comparative analysis on techniques of different domains is conducted to evaluate the performance within doubly selective fading Rayleigh channels". Own simulated data (Table I: 16000 training and 2000 testing samples); no code or data link appears in the paper.
notes: Included, area 4: OTFS channel estimation in the delay-Doppler domain with a learned CNN-BGRU compensation module, then single-tap time-frequency equalization (pp. 2-4). Title on page 1 matches the DOI. q1: EVA and ETU are not 3GPP TR 38.901 models; marked 1 under the other-standardized-model rule for reviewer confirmation, and the training channel is not stated. q2: train 30 dB and test 0 to 30 dB is an SNR sweep; speed and profile sweeps are not stated as held out. q3: the TF baseline is derived from LSTM-based [5], inferred from the reference title (p. 5) and the offline-training entry of Table II; Section IV never says LSTM. Table I, Table II and Fig. 5 were read from page images (pp. 4-5).
